question.value: Is there jet-ISM interaction in the host of the lensed quasar MG J0414+0534 at z=2.639, as seen in resolved continuum and CO(11-10) at ~50 pc resolution?

evidence.quote: In ALMA Cycle 4, we proposed carrying out long baseline observations of the CO(11-10) line to probe the distribution and kinematics of molecular gas surrounding quasar jets on small scales.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spws centered at 335.370, 337.120, 347.182, 348.995 GHz, 1.875 GHz bandwidth each, 0.976563 MHz channels, 1920 channels

evidence.quote: four spectral windows centered at 335.370, 337.120, 347.182, and 348.995 GHz, with a bandwidth 1.875 GHz (frequency domain mode)
The maximum and minimum baselines were 13.8944 km and 113 m, respectively.
The achieved angular resolutions are $0.03\ensuremath{''}-0.04\ensuremath{''}$ and $\sim 0.07\ensuremath{''}$, respectively.
the total on-source integrating times were 38.72, 39.00, 40.65, and 38.88 minutes, respectively.
Our ALMA Cycle 4 observations were carried out on 2017 November 1, 8, 10, and 11.

flux_scale_uncertainty.value: Cycle 2 vs 4 amplitude difference below ~10% in uv range 140-1400 m

evidence.quote: It turned out that the difference is below $\sim 10\%$, which is comparable to the typical error value in ALMA observations.

self_calibration.value: Phase-only, Cycle 2 and 4 separately, spws combined, S/N>=3.0 (S/N>2.0 for Cycle 4 three-antenna solutions)

evidence.quote: we carried out phase-only self-calibration for our previous Cycle 2 (cite: inoue2017) and new Cycle 4 data, separately.
by reducing the condition for rejecting solutions for a group of three antennas to S/N $>2.0$

weighting_robust.value: Briggs robust=0.5 for continuum; natural for CO

evidence.quote: The continuum and CO images were obtained with a Briggs ($robust=0.5$) and a natural weightings, respectively.

continuum_subtraction.value: uv-plane subtraction for Cycles 2 and 4, then combined with inverse-variance weights

evidence.quote: We also subtracted the continuum emission from the line channels for both the Cycles 2 and 4 data in the $uv$ plane

array_combination.value: Cycle 2 and 4 combined with weights inversely proportional to error variance

evidence.quote: we combined the continuum data with weights inversely proportional to the variance of errors.

evidence.quote: The channel maps of the lensed CO(11-10) emission were generated with a width of 146 MHz (125.6 $\textrm{km}\,\textrm{s}^{-1}$) per channel.

analysis_steps.goal: Self-calibrate and combine Cycle 2 and 4 data

method.value: Phase-only self-cal each dataset, continuum subtraction in uv, inverse-variance weighted combination

evidence.quote: we combined the continuum data with weights inversely proportional to the variance of errors.
sufficient signal-to-noise ratio (S/N $\geq 3.0$) for each gain solution

validation.value: Dynamic range rose ~120 to ~250 (Cycle 2); 140 (Cycle 4); amplitude comparison <~10%

evidence.quote: The ’dynamic range,’ defined as peak intensity per root-mean-square (rms) error, increased from $\sim 120$ to $\sim 250$.

method.value: SIE+cored isothermal sphere+shear background model fit to HST/VLBI/MIR constraints; subhalo perturbations fit with ALMA continuum; de-lensed images from linear combination of A1, A2, B

evidence.quote: Using the best-fit lensing model, we reconstructed de-lensed images of the continuum and CO(11-10) line from a linear combination of three de-lensed images of A1, A2 and B.

fitting.value: Minimizing differences between de-lensed images with astrometric/magnification constraints

evidence.quote: We obtained a best-fit model by minimizing the differences between the de-lensed images

validation.value: Residual position errors <0.003'' below HST errors

evidence.quote: The residual errors in the relative positions are $<0.003\ensuremath{''}$

analysis_steps.goal: Subtract bright core PSFs in continuum

method.value: Subtract best-fit Gaussians at lensed p and q images with flux ratios fixed to VLBI; amplitudes chosen by visual smoothness

evidence.quote: The absolute amplitudes were determined appropriately through visual inspection of the smoothness of the image in which the fitted Gaussian PSFs are subtracted off.

analysis_steps.goal: CO moment maps and PV diagram

method.value: Pixels with S/N>2 in -700<V<800 km/s; velocity zero at core q (z_CO=2.6381); PV along line through s,p,r,q fitted by chi2 minimization

evidence.quote: we only picked up pixels with S/N $>2$ within the velocity range of $-700<V<800\,\textrm{km}/\textrm{s}$ and combined them.
using $\chi^2$ minimization (Fig. [3](#f3)d)

findings_qualitative.value: Continuum and CO(11-10) show bimodal structure aligned with VLBI jet components; CO moves up to ±600 km/s at ~80 pc from core.

evidence.quote: The CO gas in the vicinity of both the eastern and western jet components at the location of $\sim 80\,$pc from the quasar core are moving at high velocities

claims.hypothesis: Jets interact with ISM in the host of MG J0414+0534
claims.experiment: De-lensed continuum and CO(11-10) maps and PV diagram along jets
claims.result: Bimodal structure aligned with jets; velocities up to ±600 km/s near jet components

evidence.quote: The observed features show clear evidence of strong interaction between the jets and interstellar medium (ISM).

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas is hot and dense
claims.experiment: RADEX modelling of CO line ratios

evidence.quote: These facts indicate that the molecular gas in MG J0414+0534 is in high-temperature and high-density conditions.

claims.hypothesis: Source is a young radio source
claims.experiment: Compare jet scale, interaction and GPS SED
claims.finding: Possibly early stage of quasar radio activity

evidence.quote: we conclude that MG J0414+0534 is possibly in the early stage of quasar radio activity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Asymmetric velocity gradient not explained by a simple circular rotating disk or spheroid.

evidence.quote: Such an asymmetric feature cannot be explained by a simple circular rotating disk or a spheroid.
Though not conclusive, our result suggests that *q* corresponds to quasar circumnuclear dust emission or synchrotron radiation

referee_caveats_inferred: Lens model uncertainty propagates to de-lensed kinematics
Line ratio modelling is crude and with single-zone assumptions
